spatial_claims.claim: ABDC is a circle with center E; BC is a diameter; AD is a non-diameter chord
EA, EB, EC, ED are all radii of the circle, so EA = EB and ED = EC
AD does not pass through E (since AD is not a diameter), so E, A, D form a triangle
E lies on diameter BC between B and C, so BC = BE + EC
EH is perpendicular to chord AD from center E; EK is perpendicular to chord FG from center E
H lies on AD at its midpoint (AH = HD); K lies on FG at its midpoint (FK = KG)
EH < EK because AD is nearer to the center than FG
Triangle EHA is right-angled at H (H on chord AD, EH perpendicular to AD)
Triangle EKF is right-angled at K (K on chord FG, EK perpendicular to FG)

configuration_map: Center E is interior to circle ABDC and lies on diameter BC at its midpoint (between B and C). Points A, B, C, D, F, G are on the circle. Chord AD does not pass through E, making E-A-D a proper triangle. H is the foot of the perpendicular from E to chord AD, lying on AD at its midpoint. K is the foot of the perpendicular from E to chord FG, lying on FG at its midpoint. EH < EK since AD is nearer to center. Right triangles EHA (at H) and EKF (at K) share equal hypotenuses (radii AE = EF).
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof uses the Pythagorean theorem (I.47) on right triangles formed by center-perpendicular-chord endpoint configurations, avoiding any angle decomposition. Key spatial facts — E on diameter between B and C, E not on non-diameter chords, perpendicular from center bisecting chords, right triangles with radii as hypotenuses — are all compatible. No inside/outside contradictions, no betweenness conflicts, and no invalid angle sums.
